gem:westfjords.desc: Látrabjarg is a promontory in the Westfjords of Iceland, and the westernmost point in Iceland. The cliffs are home to millions of birds, including puffins, northern gannets, guillemots and razorbills. It is vital for their survival as it hosts up to 40% of the world population for some species such as the razorbill.

gem:westfjords.name: Isafjordur
gem:westfjords.desc: The lively capital of the Westfjords set on a dramatic fjord spit

gem:westfjords.name: Raudisandur
gem:westfjords.desc: Rauðisandur is a coastal area in Westfjords, Iceland. Historically it was located in the historic Vestur-Barðastrandarsýsla county.

gem:westfjords.name: Hornstrandir
gem:westfjords.desc: Hornstrandir is Iceland's northernmost peninsula, covering 580 km2 (220 sq mi) at the northern end of the Westfjords, to the north of the Jökulfirðir and to the northwest of Drangajökull glacier.

gem:westfjords.name: Vigur
gem:westfjords.desc: Vigur is the second largest island of the Ísafjarðardjúp fjord in Westfjords, Iceland. Located just south of the Arctic Circle, the island is around 2 kilometres (6,600 ft) in length and 400 metres (1,300 ft) in width. The island is most noted for its thriving seabird colonies, traditional eiderdown production, and historical buildings.

gem:westfjords.name: Drangajokull
gem:westfjords.desc: Drangajökull is the northernmost glacier of Iceland, occupying the southern foothills of the Hornstrandir peninsula in the Westfjords region. It covers approximately 150 km2 and is the only Icelandic ice cap situated entirely below 1,000 metres in elevation. Lake sediment cores show that Drangajökull persisted near or above its present extent well into the mid-Holocene before retreating to near-modern limits between about 9,500 and 7,200 years ago.

gem:westfjords.name: Bolungarvik
gem:westfjords.desc: Bolungarvík is a small town and the only built-up area in the municipality of Bolungarvíkurkaupstaður in the northwest of Iceland, located on the Westfjords peninsula, approximately 14 km (8.7 mi) from the town of Ísafjörður and 473 km (294 mi) from the capital city Reykjavík.

gem:westfjords.name: Osvor Maritime Museum
gem:westfjords.desc: A recreated 19th-century fishing station with turf huts and salting hut

gem:westfjords.name: Thingeyri
gem:westfjords.desc: The oldest trading post in the Westfjords on Dyrafjordur fjord

gem:westfjords.name: Flateyri
gem:westfjords.desc: Flateyri is a village situated in Iceland's Westfjords. It is part of the municipality of Ísafjarðarbær and has a population of approximately 200, making it the largest settlement in Önundarfjörður.

gem:westfjords.name: Sudureyri
gem:westfjords.desc: Suðureyri is a small Icelandic fishing village perched on the tip of the 13 km-long Súgandafjörður in the Westfjords.

gem:westfjords.name: Patreksfjordur
gem:westfjords.desc: Patreksfjörður is a fishing village in the Westfjords of Iceland. It was an important fishing and trading post until the Icelandic government's introduction of a fishing quota in 1990. Administratively, it is part of the municipality of Vesturbyggð.

gem:westfjords.name: Bildudalur
gem:westfjords.desc: Bíldudalur is a village situated on the coast of Arnarfjörður, one of the Westfjords in Iceland.
